articleTitle: COSPAS-SARSAT satellite system
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: COSPAS-SARSAT is an international satellite system designed to assist search and rescue operations using distress beacons operating on 121.5 MHz or 406 MHz and providing alert and location data to rescue coordination centres (RCCs). The system objective is to serve all organizations in the world with responsibility for search and rescue (SAR) operations, whether at sea, in the air, or on land. The COSPAS-SARSAT system was jointly developed and established by Russia (formerly the USSR), USA, Canada and France. The cooperation of the countries involved proceeded under the Memorandum of Understanding, signed in 1979. Following extensive testing and operation, an "International COSPAS-SARSAT Programme Agreement" was signed on 1 July 1988 in Paris by the governments of Russia, USA, Canada and France. This agreement established a framework for long-term operation of the system. The COSPAS-SARSAT system is used by all member states of the International Maritime Organization and the International Civil Aviation Organization. By May 1998 26 countries and/or competent organizations had officially joined the COSPAS-SARSAT programme.

articleTitle: CHERNOMOR satellite communication system
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: A group of Russian Space Agency enterprises has proposed the CHERNOMOR multifunctional interconnected satellite communication system. In this system groups of satellites are launched into geostationary as well as middle- and low-altitude orbits, thus exploiting each system's advantages. Users can therefore receive a wide spectrum of satellite communication services. The realization of the proposed system has been optimized in terms of its technical and economic parameters. Satellites will be launched into orbits from Russian territory by modernized strategic missiles that will allow the launch price to be reduced considerably. Satellite groupings are formed based on middle-altitude satellites (8-12 broadband channels /spl times/36 MHz) of any necessary configuration in the FSS (fixed satellite service) frequency range. Increasing the satellite resources in each orbit can be achieved by launching a new satellite with repeaters having the necessary new frequency range. This system will have significant economic advantages as well as reduced costs and technical risks concerning realization. The operational system will allow all credits to be repaid, will make a profit and will use the proceeds for system development. The CHERNOMOR system is designed to consist of separate components, each of which can be put into operation independently, subject to the availability of investment, and the requirements of different users. Therefore compatibility of the system and ground networks is secured.

articleTitle: X-band power amplifier for active phased-array antennas
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: An amplifier is designed with P/sub 1/ /sub dB/>2 W and gain >30 dB in the frequency band of 8.1/spl plusmn/0.25 GHz. The gain variation is less than 1 dB, with controlled phase from 0/spl deg/ to 360/spl deg/, and efficiency of more than 20%. As an active element base we use crystals of the transistors A/spl Pi/608 and A/spl Pi/603, produced by the Pulsar plant.

articleTitle: Satellite communication and broadcasting systems in the 21st century
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: There has been much technical progress and development in all areas of technology over recent years. The information society, satellite communication and broadcasting are part of this process, and have become a characteristic of the second half of the 20th century. In the global information infrastructure (GII) today, the space segment, on the one hand, plays an integrating role, and on the other, provides an opportunity for individual flexible access to information resources. Obviously the GII will play a leading role in economic development and the well-being of citizens in the 21st century in those countries which are actively participating in it's development. Currently there are many projects for creating new satellite communication and broadcasting systems, with the operation of these systems planned for the beginning of the 21st century.

articleTitle: Hyperlong medium adaptive multiple access with dynamic control of the traffic and service quality for mobile satellite ATM networks
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: Summary form only given. Promising prospects for the transition to integrated broadband information technologies in the 21st Century i.e. B-ISDN, B-Internet, multimedia services etc. are dependent on the development of ATM. Impressive results concerning the establishment of high-speed ATM transport lines, platforms and fixed access networks with centralized architectures have already been achieved. However centralized ATM architectures are used mainly in transport and corporate networks as their cost is unacceptable for deployment in mass public networks. The key problem on the way to integrated broadband ATM public networks is the implementation of inexpensive distributed ATM systems for access to broadband integrated services. Active elaboration of such 3rd generation wireless (WLAN) and mobile broadband (MBS, WATM) systems with radio coverage of highly urbanized local areas is being conducted within the framework of the European ACTS Program. The universal adaptive method of ATM access to various hyperlong media and efficient methods concerning dynamic control of bandwidth distribution, traffic parameters and service quality which provide an increase in radio coverage up to the size of metropolitan (MAN), wide-area (WAN) and satellite (GM PCS) networks are discussed. The architectural basis of universal multifunctional ATM networks for subscriber access to B-ISDN, B-Internet, multimedia services on radio, optical, optical-fiber and satellite channels with flexible and distributed architecture is developed on the basis of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Data services in the Inmarsat communication system
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: Quite a number of data services are available in the Inmarsat communications system, from low-speed store and forward up to full duplex high speed 64 or 56 Kbit/s real-time data services. The data services are available from practically anywhere and do not require any infrastructure except power supply for the Inmarsat terminal which can be a car battery or solar panels and a direct line of vision to one of the satellites. The integrity of the information which goes through the system is achieved by using forward error correction (FEC) procedures. In medium-speed data services ARQ/V.42 procedures are available in addition to FEC. Data services are the basis for implementation of different widely used applications, though in quite a number of cases when using specific solutions built taking into account the specific features of the Inmarsat channels the effectiveness of the utilisation of resources can be higher. The connection of a computer to a new digital satellite terminal is effected directly as to a modem and there is no need to use any modems anymore. Basic and extended (to control specific parameters) sets of AT commands are available.

articleTitle: Ka-band LNA MIC
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: We present results of the design and fabrication of Ka-band LNA MIC, for radioastronomical equipment. The parameters of the amplifier are: working band of frequencies 33-36 GHz, noise figure <3.4 dB, gain >20 dB, /spl Delta/gain <1.5 dB, power characteristic (1 dB) >8 dBm. The amplifier is intended for working in hermetically sealed equipment. The amplifier size is 21.5/spl times/12/spl times/5 mm. The amplifier is made with GaAs HEMT, developed by SRI "Pulsar".

articleTitle: Satellite paging: state of the art and development trends
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: This review gives the current state and development perspective of satellite paging on the basis of exploitation of satellite systems. SPS Iridium shows the technology of collection of messages from senders and principle of transferring them to satellite pagers. This is the first experience of creating nodes of collection of paging messages from senders by using the Internet through OOO "Page-Link Technology" as the first service-provider of the satellite paging system IRIDIUM. We give brief characteristics and possibilities of satellite pagers.

articleTitle: The global satellite mobile system
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: A global mobile telephone system using middle Earth orbit satellites-responders is discussed. The principles of the system construction and its main characteristics are described.

articleTitle: Aspects of using satellite communications in distance learning
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: Modern telecommunication technologies on the one hand raise the problem of quality of education and, on the other hand, allow us to change greatly traditional methods and procedures of education. This paper reviews satellite delivery of courses.

articleTitle: To comparative evaluation of efficiency of the satellite communications systems using various orbits
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: This paper considers the limit relationship between the capacities of a separate transponder (beam) satellite, a multibeam transponder satellite and a multisatellite PCS, depending on their orbit altitudes for a number of significant cases. These cases include identical output in the beam or in the entire transponder satellite when the altitudes are different, and the apertures of the onboard multibeam antennas are identical or when the beam partial areas on the surface of the Earth are identical. The parameters mentioned, in their turn, determine the relationship of the power-mass characteristics, and, accordingly, costs of creating the orbital groupings. By comparing the latter with the capacities, it becomes possible to comparatively evaluate the specific costs for the transmission of an information unit, depending on the orbital altitude, number of satellites in the system, and the beams of the transponder-satellites.

articleTitle: "KUPON" spacecraft of "Bankir" satellite communication and data transmitting system
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The "KUPON" spacecraft is designed for data retranslation (data transmission, telefax, telephone) between subscribers of the satellite communication network. It was developed for the "Bankir" satellite communication and data transmitting system of the Central Bank of Russian Federation. The spacecraft was designed on the basis of the Lavochkin satellite communications. That has led to a decrease in terms of development and tests, cost of the spacecrafts and the entire communication system as well. The covering zone is formed by three S/C of the orbital system, each of them having on-board retranslation complexes (BRTK) working in Ku-band (14/11 GHz). Active phased antenna grids (AFAR) that can form up to 16 narrow receiving-transmitting beams, that can be retargeted to any undersatellite point in the limit of the S/C viewing area, are used, giving a possibility of changing the covering zones in the limits of the viewing area and to have flexible redistribution of the retranslator working ability. S/C injection into the staying points is performed by the three-staged "Proton" launch vehicle with the upper stage "DM" from the Baikonour launch site. In order to solve tasks of the on-board systems and also to perform control, diagnostics and recovery of the on-board systems, there is an on-board control complex (BKU), and in order to provide normal functioning of the BKU and BRTK for the execution of the input before the S/C tasks, there is an on-board control complex of service systems (BKOS).

articleTitle: The solution of fundamental problems of electrocommunication as reliable way of winning the market of informational technologies
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The stock holding company "International Concern of Satellite Communication" (KOSS) was incorporated in 1991 as the organizational structure which combined the scientists and leading specialists of a number of enterprises of the former military industrial complex of the CIS countries. The rich intellectual and technical potential of KOSS allows us not only to carry out research and development but also to realize complicated applications in the field of radio electronic, communication systems and instruments engineering. KOSS has the corresponding state licenses for the realization of state orders.

articleTitle: The ways of forming the single-valued scale for the space station phase radio goniometer
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The single-valued scale formed in multichannel phase radio gonimeters used for short range navigation can be obscured by space station construction features. This work examines the problems of forming single-valued scales in a wide range of angles for the phase radio goniometers. Algorithms for forming the single-valued scales are suggested and different structure schemes for radio goniometers are presented.

articleTitle: A base laser terminal for space communication
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The Scientific-Industrial Corporation on Space Instruments is carrying out research and design activities for the purpose of creating a base laser terminal with capacity up to 2 Gbit/s that will be able to meet the various requirements of LEO spacecraft and satellite systems. This paper presents the principles forming the basis of such a terminal and describes the main technologies used. Completion of the full-scale on-ground tests is planned as well as the commencement of the flight tests on MIR orbital space station using a downlink at rates up to 128 Mbit/s and an uplink at a rate of 2.66 Mbit/s.

articleTitle: About simplification of the procedure of legal registration of import licence and allowance for the maintenance of small ground station for satellite communication
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: We review some innovations in the procedure of obtaining legal documents for import and maintenance of small ground stations for satellite communications with 3.8 m and smaller antennas (including VSAT).

articleTitle: Low and medium Earth orbit satellite systems: spheres application, services and customers
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: As the direction of developments in mobile communication networks has been changing, the efforts of operators of ground and satellite systems of mobile communication has been uniting. Thus the scope of services in this sphere has been increasing continuously. This fact has given us ground to suppose that the market for mobile communication services in Russia, as it was estimated in 1995, has scope to increase further.

articleTitle: On the implementation of software-only videoconferencing codec on PC
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: Intensive recent progress in computer technologies has stimulated new solutions for transmission of audio and video information in digital form, The transmission of digital video and audio signals through channels of restricted capacity, such as switched public telephone lines, mobile radio systems, local computer networks, Internet and satellite telecommunications attract a constantly growing interest. The bit rate in such lines available for transmission of audio and video information is limited dependent upon particular application in the range from 30 to 512 Kbit/s. In spite of the low bit rate digital coding itself requires significant computational resources and implies severe limitations on the performance of the real-time encoder. It should be also taken into account that for channels with low bit rate a codec must implement compression algorithms allowing us to achieve a large compression ratio and acceptable quality. Necessary compression ratios can be achieved only by means of intraframe coding as well as interframe motion compensation.

articleTitle: State, problems and perspective of satellite systems use for air traffic control in civil aviation
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The concept of technical design is given for air traffic management (ATM) in the Russian Federation (RF) on the basis of space and satellite technology. A stage by stage implementation procedure is suggested along with plans of its integration into the global aeronavigation structure.

articleTitle: Parameters' optimization of reservation's algorithms, for providing continuous connections and reassigning the channels in LEO networks
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: In a LEO (low Earth orbit) satellite communications network, connections have to be switched between satellites in the network as the satellites move in and out of radio visibility. This paper presents recommendations for reserving reception capacity on a satellite in preparation for a connection being established.

articleTitle: Implementation of satellite communication systems with the use of small-size satellites on a geostationary orbit
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The scheme of implementation of satellite communication systems using the cluster approach to development of a space segment is considered. Such an approach allows us to execute step-by-step the frequency allocation of the orbital slot by using the small-sized communication satellites. The advantages of such a scheme are presented.

articleTitle: The analysis of construction variants of onboard systems of combined signals processing
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: A perspective is given for maintenance of the requirements for interference defence in satellite communication systems, which is based on joint application of various ways of processing. The joint application of various kinds of processing permits us to overcome or to ease the number of basic restrictions which are inherent to separate methods and that application permits us to realize their potential possibilities. So, at the concurrence of the spatial spectrum of a useful signal and interference the efficiency of spatial methods of processing is low. Therefore interference suppression methods for signal processing using polarization distinction of a signal and interference are applied. The joint or combined application of processing methods permits us to provide a changing of modes of operations depending on the change of signal-interference conditions for the purpose of functioning with maximally possible quality.

articleTitle: New technological and constructive methods of raising of power irradiation and information transmission speed in the optical transmitter on the base of GaAlAs lasers for IOCL
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: This report presents results on the study and development of the first native Russian high frequency semiconductor lasers for intersatellite optical communication links (IOCL). Due to the application of the latest technology in the design of the lasers and the new method of MOCVD epitaxy developed to fabricate them, the results have important practical value. GaAlAs single mode lasers with output wavelengths in the range of 0.81-0.86 /spl mu/m, increased continuous mode radiating power up to 60-70 mW and life times in the range of 5-10 thousand hours have been created. For the first time on lasers of this type high modulation frequencies (up to 250 MHz) that allow an increased transmission information rate on each channel and meet the international standard 155 Mbit/sec (Recommendations G.703) were attained. At 100-200 MHz, the power in the pulse reached values of more than 100 mW.

articleTitle: DBS TV spacecraft "GALS-R16"
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: Telecommunication is the most important field of economic and social infrastructure of a country. The report contains information on a new generation of GALS-series communication and broadcasting satellites developed within the framework of the Russian Federal Space Program.

articleTitle: Space-time ultrawideband systems of satellite communication
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The opportunities for construction of satellite systems of digital communication on a spatio-temporal basis for superbroadband signals are analyzed with the help of antenna lattices with an ensemble of non-identical and non-equidistant channel signals is shown, so that it is possible to realize the advantages of superbroadband signals in electromagnetic compatibility, to use highly effective resonant units at formation, amplification (strengthening) of capacity, radiation and reception, and also in addition to receive spatial selectivity under the form of a total signal.

articleTitle: Program of the development of Yamal-200 and Yamal-300 communications satellites for Russian national system of fixed satellite communications
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: Satellites Yamal-200 and Yamal-300 are developed to mate the system of fixed communications and TV broadcasting of the Russian Federation as a substitution of Horizont and Express satellites. This paper presents the key organizational aspects of the project, which are non-traditional in domestic practice. The project is being developed cooperatively by home enterprises headed by RSC Energia with the participation of leading forcing manufacturers NEC (Japan) and DASA (Germany). The state customers are RSA and Russian Satellite Communications Company (RSCC). The investor as well as prime contractor for the payloads is JSC Gascom. The Yamal satellites provide the United Communication Network (UCN) of RF, and service provision in the world market of satellite communications services. The principles of succession with the existing national "Horizont" and "Express" networks are mentioned, along with key features of the satellites, and main parameters of the payloads. In their manufacturing they use modern engineering solutions and parts, which allow us to achieve the same characteristics as the best foreign satellites. The service zones are shown, maximally adapted to RF territory to allow the provision of high-quality services. The paper contains the capacity characteristics and the list of services to be provided by Yamal satellites, the parameters of the communications and TV ground stations to support the mentioned traffic, and the key features of Yamal satellites in comparison with foreign analogues.

articleTitle: LEO-system: how to select launchers and scenarios for rational deployment and replenishment
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: Presently commercial low-Earth orbit satellite systems are being developed. The first constellations such as Iridium, Globalstar, Teledesic are to come into operation over the next few years, some satellites being placed into orbits. Possible launch and satellite failures as well as scheduled replacement and potential augmentation of a constellation would require further launches. So a new and rather significant segment of the launch services market is now emerging. The LEO-system deployment needs launchers which will be capable of placing several satellites into the same or different orbit planes.

articleTitle: MM radio-wave generators of stochastic oscillations for the hidden communications system
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: Systems of radiocommunications for sending complex noise signals have many serious advantages. In this work the principal attention was given to methods of SO excitation both on volumetric and on surface waves in systems with wear and strong resonance based on BWT and a generator with surface wave resonator (SWR). We consider many-beam nonlinear structures on the basis of SWR with lagging of the system reaction at the beginning of the nonlinearity effect fast wave. It is shown that scenario transition from order to chaos has a universal character and is called forth by effects of electrons regrouping in a wave field of large amplitude. The appearance of SO is connected with a sequence of bifurcation cycles of double the period of automodulation of the distributed autooscillating system (DAS). By changing the velocity and density of the power electron beam we realize control parameters of the oscillation spectrum.

articleTitle: VSAT networks of Russian Satellite Communications Company
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The Russian Satellite Communications Company (RSCC) is a national space communications operator and has three decades of experience in this field. The Russian Satellite Communications Company offers its customers the following services: provision of space segment capacity including long-term lease of the satellite transponders; provision of Earth stations services for organizing satellite communications channels; television and radio transmission-reception in analog and digital mode; organisation of voice and data services in international, national and regional networks in analog and digital modes; videoconferencing services; transmission of newspaper matrices; telecommunication services during international space missions; satellite communications Earth station supply, installation, commissioning and maintenance services all over the Russian territory; satellite communications Earth station approval services; satellite communications dedicated network set-up services; provision of access to the Internet on IP protocol to remote customers. The VSAT network enables us to link remote users within a single digital communications network featuring service integration.

articleTitle: The reliability multimodel forecasting of the communication satellite equipment
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: A method of forecasting of a residual resource of complex technical systems using the example of a communication satellite based on the application of the multimodel approach for forecasting the parameters of the satellite equipment is considered.

articleTitle: INTERSPUTNIK's development prospects on the eve of the XXIst century
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The Moscow-based INTERSPUTNIK International Organization of Space Communications is an international intergovernmental organization using a global satellite communications system. It was founded in 1971 in order to provide services to any users without discrimination or limitation of rights including cases when a customer is a member or user of a different international satellite communications system. At present there are 23 member-countries and more than 100 users, state and private companies. INTERSPUTNIK provides satellite communication services, including television, telephony, data transmission, videoconferencing, VSAT etc., both in analog and digital modes. The Organization provides communication in global, regional and domestic networks, having South and South-East Asia, Russia and other CIS countries, Central and Eastern Europe as principal users. Broadcasting and telecommunication companies as well as service providers are among the principal users of INTERSPUTNIK. The INTERSPUTNIK system consists of a space segment, which includes communication satellites owned by the Russian Federation (like Gorizont, Express, Gals) and a ground complex, which includes Earth stations owned by states or recognized operators. At present, there are more than 70 stations, located in different parts of the world, operating in the INTERSPUTNIK system.

articleTitle: Modern microwave range integrated circuits based on GaAs and its solid solutions
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The object of this report is to show some achievements and development problems of domestic integrated semiconductor microwave electronics on the basis of practical experiment and achievements, stored in the Scientific-Research Institute for Microdevices of the NPO ELAS. Attention was given to questions related to integrated microwave electronics use in the space microelectronic apparato-building, in satellite communications systems and Earth remote sensing from space.

articleTitle: Monitoring system for satellite stations network
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: A monitoring system for a satellite station network, "Monitor", is presented. System capabilities and hardware used are described. Program results in graphical form and screen snapshots are also included.

articleTitle: Latest developments at ESA in the area of telecommunications and navigation
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The spectacular growth of the satellite telecommunications market is today generated mostly by private investments, which are already larger than the governmental ones. Up to now, almost 70 telecommunications satellites have been produced by European satellite manufacturers, who hold almost 30% of the telecommunication satellite market and represent today the only alternative to USA industry. Telecommunications satellites represent more than 90% of the customer base for Arianespace, Europe's world leader in space transportation that has captured half of the international commercial market. The proliferation of television would have been impossible without the fleet of over 150 satellites on the geostationary orbit. The average European spends a tenth of his life in front of a TV set watching ten, twenty, fifty or more programmes for entertainment, training and information. Together, these European TV channels have combined advertisement revenues exceeding 15 billion ECU per year.

articleTitle: Avia-space means for deployment and support of orbital communication systems
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The requirements for satellite launch of orbital communication systems are considered in this article. The multi-purpose Avia-space system currently being developed in Russia is discussed. This system will be commercially profitable and provide rapid deployment and servicing of telecommunication satellite systems.

articleTitle: Noise immunity comparative assessment of personal satellite communication systems equipped with code sealing and using various relays
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: Personal communication systems on the basis of low orbital satellites is a quickly developing telecommunication field. One may forecast that low orbital personal satellite communication systems (LOPSCS) together with computer technology as two closely connected key elements will benefit. However the noise immunity level in the LOPSCS depends not only on the applied signal structure but also on the optimal level of the channels to process them (receivers and particularly relays). Therefore we shall focus on comparison of the two main types of relays: transparent relays and relays with onboard signal processing.

articleTitle: Application of methods of combined signal processing in systems of mobile communication
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: A combined system of processing (CSP) is presented for the improvement of the characteristics of mobile communication systems. It is shown that at the expense of the introduction of the CSP system into the signal processing structure of the base stations (BS), an increase in capacity of the system is provided.

articleTitle: Radio space complex for gas and oil mains corrosion monitoring
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The developed Pulsar-1 complex provides gas mains corrosion monitoring (CM) which comprises a complex system of measures aimed at decreasing the thermodynamic probability of corrosion destruction of metal construction elements, and includes means and methods of anti-corrosion protection, sensor devices for corrosion control, measuring equipment, as well as a system of collection, processing, and transmitting of information used for on-line control of protection means.

articleTitle: The ROSTELESAT multifunctional space telecommunication system (MSTS)
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The ROSTELESAT multifunctional space telecommunication system (MSTS) is designed for establishing mobile and fixed satellite communication channels for digital information reception and transmission between the mobile and fixed users to provide public community, government and commercial organizations with services in global digital voice communication and data transmission in any geographical area of the world, including poorly populated, remote and hardly reached regions of Russia. Telephony, facsimile messages and data transmission are provided with rates from 1.2 up to 64 Kbit/s, along with the latest multimedia and computer services, including communication between computer networks of various levels. Similar information transmission could be done with up to 2048 Kbit/s standard rates; data in Earth remote sounding (investigation of natural resources, supervision over dynamic processes on the Earth surface and in the atmosphere etc.) with actual real-time data acquisition and processing.

articleTitle: Radically new technology for manufacturing components and units of satellite communication systems
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: A set of millimeter wave components and devices made by multilayer electroforming is presented. It is shown that the proposed technology makes possible quasi-monolithic multifunctional devices for communication facilities.

articleTitle: High-power units for GALS R16 transponders
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The basic design principles and performance of the high-power units for the GALS R16 transponders are presented. An overview is given which details the activities at Dornier Satellitensysteme GmbH for improved TWTA for future satellite transponders. The mission of the GALS R16 spacecraft is the support of the Russian Ku-band TV network which allows simple and low-cost on-ground subscriber units using antennas of 60 cm to 90 cm diameter. This requires a satellite EIRP of 51 dBW. To achieve the required radiated field strength, travelling wave tube amplifiers (TWTA) at power levels of 100 W at the end of life (EOL) are used in the 24 transponder channels (4:6 redundancy). Common design activities of JSC INFORMCOSMOS, SPAR Aerospace and Dornier Satellitensysteme GmbH led to a TWTA design which meets the Russian spacecraft requirement and achieves the most perfect features achieved during recent space programs executed by Dornier. Additional transponder equipment as waveguide isolators and switches are built by COMDEV Canada and supplied by SPAR Aerospace. The TWTA are designed, integrated and tested by Dornier using TWTA supplied by TTEG (former AEG) Germany and electrical power conditioners (EPC) developed, space-qualified and manufactured by Dornier Satellitensysteme GmbH, Germany.

articleTitle: Software package for creation of Earth surface digital elevation matrix use radar remote sensing data
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The subject of this report is the description of a software package for the processing of remote sensing synthetic aperture radar (SAR) which provides, in particular, the decision of the task relief elevation restoration and creation of digital maps of a terrestrial surface. The results of this software package can be used in communication line design and replacement of the elements of communication systems, and calculation of the zones of radiovisibility.

articleTitle: Synchronous code division of subscriber's stations in satellite systems of personal radio communication
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: For satellite personal systems of communication with synchronous code division of subscriber stations on a spread spectrum complex signal basis the optimization of a set of the quality parameters of the resulting complex signals, both in subscriber stations and interface stations, is done, and the principles of processing of these signals are developed.

articleTitle: Yamal satellite communication and broadcast system
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: Management of such a large company as Gasprom is a complex task requiring permanent broadening of the sphere of application and updating of the information technologies. Having this in mind, since the 1990s Gasprom's top managers have been working towards modernization and updating of its technological communication network (TCN) on a modern technical basis. Gasprom communications network, one of the biggest in Russia, includes 78,000 km of inter-city wire and radio links, 540 communications centers, millions of kilometers of channels and paths, and more than 7000 skilled communication specialists. One of the most important aspects of network modernization (side by side with improvement of wire and radio links) is the development of the Yamal satellite communications and broadcast system (SCBS) which nowadays satisfies not only production requirements but also the social needs of the inhabitants and people working in gas areas.

articleTitle: Application of system Sky-Frame in telecommunication network of JSC "Coal-Telecom"
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: SkyFrame (SF) can be considered a "hybrid" technology. It takes the best of DAMA (demand assigned multiple access), TDMA (time division multiple access) and SCPC (single channel per carrier or point-to-point) technology and fills a niche application that the other three technologies cannot. SkyFrame is ideal for small to medium size corporate networks that require cost effective efficient support of both voice and data. SkyFrame, unlike the other three technologies, is frame relay based, and as such it is ideally suited to the "bursty" nature of LAN traffic. This cannot be said for the other three technologies. SkyFrame is designed to bridge the gap between small and large networks that have a mix of voice and data. Current star/TDMA and mesh/DAMA offerings cannot economically scale down to small-and-medium size networks. SkyFrame addresses the low-end TDMA and DAMA market while addressing all of the SCPC market; both low and high-end applications.

articleTitle: Control system of the network satellite data communication system
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: In view of the International Union of Electronic Communication (CCITT) recommendations, the structure of the control system for the satellite data communication system AS Sirena-3 has been developed. The purpose of the control system is to increase the network efficiency performance, decrease the cost of the provided communication services and minimize network operation costs.

articleTitle: Average power millimeter-wave band TWT with the coupled cavities
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The results of research and development of average power eight-millimeter band TWT with cylindrical coupled cavities (CCC) with positive inductive coupling are given. The influence of geometrical dimensions on bandwidth, amplification factor, single and double section TWT of millimeter-waveband (MWB) efficiency are investigated. The pack design of experimental TWT with output power of 5 W and amplification factor of 30 dB is described.

articleTitle: Preparation of input data for algorithm to control by HRA beam
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: This paper describes the methods for preparation of input data for an interpolation algorithm for real-time phase control of a hybrid reflector antenna (HRA) beam via an iterative method of phase synthesis. To be dependent on the required class of formed radiated patterns in a survey sector, the proposed methods can include several steps for correcting the input data.

articleTitle: Development of a dual-frequency GPS/GLONASS receiver for space application
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: Laboratory breadboards of a high precision dual-frequency Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver have been developed at the Institute of Satellite Navigation at the University of Leeds (ISN) under a European Space Agency (ESA) programme. The main objective of these breadboards is to serve as development tools for receiver signal processing research in view of the scientific applications of GNSS. Some of these applications will be realised by means of receivers embarked on satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) as part of on-going and future ESA programmes and will include precise orbit determination, radio occultation measurements and measurements of the parameters characterising GNSS signals reflected at the sea surface. During an occultation measurement the GNSS signal propagation encounters a challenging environment. Not only substantial Doppler dynamics occur during a measurement due to the effect of gradients of the refraction index, but also attenuation and deep fading caused by multipath propagation. The signal tracking requirements for space applications are analysed and applied to the hardware and software tasks. Resultant enhancements to the receiver digital processing are presented along with their impact on the intended application. The areas of concern are the acquisition and tracking of signals in high dynamics and at low carrier-to-noise ratios (CNR), and on improving the performance of tracking the GPS P code without full knowledge of the spreading code.

articleTitle: Earth stations coordinates definition in satellite communications systems
publicationTitle: 3rd International Conference on Satellite Communications (IEEE Cat. No.98TH8392)
abstract: The coordinate definition of the subscribers in communication systems of mobile satellite service (MSS) with widely used transparent signal relaying is possible in several ways. Among them is an obvious process to use in GPS/GLONASS technology, direct measurements of the slant range user station up to the satellite, application of reference (checkpoint) Earth sites in combination with range measurements or Doppler methods etc. It is essential that the legal user's terminal of the communication system service, as the regular components of a MSS system, one way or the other participates in procedures of its coordinate-definition, that sharply simplifies their process engineering, raises accuracy and ensures a wholesale (large-scale) queuing service for the subscribers.
